chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the demented woman whose intellect has gone, is her selling and her charity allowed? He said: No. And about the divorce of the intoxicated man and his emancipation, he said: It is not allowed.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of divorce and emancipation for an intoxicated man in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the legal status of those with impaired cognition, specifically ruling that a demented woman cannot be sold or give charity, and an intoxicated man's divorce and emancipation are invalid. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that valid legal acts require soundness of mind (aql), excluding those whose reasoning is temporarily or permanently compromised. The ruling underscores the protection of property and family rights for individuals lacking full legal capacity.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the demented woman with the intellect gone, is her selling and her charity allowed?’ He<sup>asws</sup>; ‘No’. And about a divorce by the intoxicated and his emancipation, he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Not allowed’.
